conceptCapsule.title: Mathematical Formulation of Newton's Second Law & Variable Mass Dynamics
conceptCapsule.summary: Newton's second law asserts that the net external force equals the time rate of change of linear momentum: $\vec{F} = \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt} = \frac{d(m\vec{v})}{dt} = m\frac{d\vec{v}}{dt} + \vec{v}_{\text{rel}}\frac{dm}{dt}$. For constant mass systems, $\vec{F} = m\vec{a}$. For variable mass systems: (1) Conveyor belt / sand feeding: $F_{\text{ext}} = v\frac{dm}{dt}$, Power supplied $P = Fv = v^2\frac{dm}{dt}$. (2) Rocket propulsion: $F_{\text{thrust}} = u_{\text{rel}}\frac{dm}{dt}$. (3) Water jet impact: Normal force $F = \rho A v^2$ (inelastic) or $F = 2\rho A v^2$ (elastic reflection).
conceptCapsule.keyFormula: $$\vec{F} = \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt}, \quad p = \sqrt{2mK}, \quad K = \frac{p^2}{2m}, \quad F_{\text{thrust}} = u_{\text{rel}}\frac{dm}{dt}, \quad F_{\text{jet}} = \rho A v^2$$
conceptCapsule.examTrap: When sand drops onto a moving conveyor belt at speed $v$, the power delivered by the motor is $P = v^2\frac{dm}{dt}$, but the rate of increase of kinetic energy of the sand is only $\frac{1}{2}v^2\frac{dm}{dt}$. The remaining 50% of the mechanical energy is inevitably dissipated as heat due to sliding friction before the sand reaches belt speed.

questions.statement: The linear momentum of a particle of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ varies with time as $\vec{p}(t) = (3t^2\hat{i} + 4t\hat{j})\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$. The magnitude of the net force acting on the particle at $t = 2\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
1. $\vec{F} = \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt} = 6t\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}\text{ N}$.
2. At $t = 2\text{ s}$: $\vec{F}(2) = 12\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}\text{ N}$.
3. Magnitude: $|\vec{F}| = \sqrt{12^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{160} = 4\sqrt{10}\text{ N} \approx 12.65\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A force $\vec{F} = (6t^2\hat{i} + 4t\hat{j})\text{ N}$ acts on a body of mass $3\text{ kg}$ initially at rest at the origin. The velocity of the body at $t = 3\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
1. $\vec{a}(t) = \frac{\vec{F}}{m} = 2t^2\hat{i} + \frac{4}{3}t\hat{j}\text{ m/s}^2$.
2. $\vec{v}(3) = \int_0^3 \left(2t^2\hat{i} + \frac{4}{3}t\hat{j}\right)dt = \left[\frac{2}{3}t^3\hat{i} + \frac{2}{3}t^2\hat{j}\right]_0^3 = 18\hat{i} + 6\hat{j}\text{ m/s}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: Water from a hose pipe of cross-sectional area $A = 10\text{ cm}^2$ strikes a vertical wall normally with a speed of $v = 15\text{ m/s}$ and falls dead down the wall without bouncing. If the density of water is $\rho = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3$, the force exerted by the water stream on the wall is:
questions.solution:
1. Mass rate: $\frac{dm}{dt} = \rho A v = 1000 \times (10 \times 10^{-4}) \times 15 = 15\text{ kg/s}$.
2. Force on wall: $F = v\frac{dm}{dt} = 15 \times 15 = 225\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: In the previous question, if the water stream bounces back elastically with the same speed from the wall, the force exerted on the wall would be:
questions.solution:
For elastic reflection, momentum change doubles: $$F = 2\rho A v^2 = 2 \times 225 = 450\text{ N}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Sand is dropped onto a conveyor belt at a constant rate of $\dfrac{dm}{dt} = 2\text{ kg/s}$. To keep the belt moving at a constant speed of $v = 3\text{ m/s}$, the extra force required to drive the belt is:
questions.solution:
Thrust force required to accelerate incoming mass to belt speed $v$: $$F = v\frac{dm}{dt} = 3 \times 2 = 6\text{ N}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: In Q5, the extra power required to keep the conveyor belt moving at constant speed $v = 3\text{ m/s}$ is:
questions.solution:
Power supplied by motor: $$P = F \times v = \left(v\frac{dm}{dt}\right)v = v^2\frac{dm}{dt} = 3^2 \times 2 = 18\text{ W}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A rocket of initial mass $M_0 = 1000\text{ kg}$ ejects gas at a constant exhaust speed $u = 500\text{ m/s}$ relative to the rocket. To give the rocket an initial upward acceleration equal to $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, the rate of consumption of fuel ($\frac{dm}{dt}$) must be:
questions.solution:
1. Rocket thrust equation: $u\frac{dm}{dt} - M_0 g = M_0 a$.
2. $500\frac{dm}{dt} = 1000(10 + 10) = 20000 \implies \frac{dm}{dt} = 40\text{ kg/s}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A machine gun fires $n = 360$ bullets per minute, each of mass $m = 20\text{ g}$, with a muzzle speed of $v = 500\text{ m/s}$. The average recoil force required to hold the gun steady in position is:
questions.solution:
1. Bullets per second $N = \frac{360}{60} = 6\text{ s}^{-1}$.
2. Average force: $F = N(mv) = 6 \times (0.02 \times 500) = 6 \times 10 = 60\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ moves along the $x$-axis such that its position is given by $x(t) = a t^2 - b t^3$. The force acting on the particle is zero at time $t$ equal to:
questions.solution:
1. $v(t) = 2at - 3bt^2$, $a(t) = 2a - 6bt$.
2. $F = ma = 0 \implies 2a - 6bt = 0 \implies t = \frac{a}{3b}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: Two bodies $A$ and $B$ have masses $m_A = 2\text{ kg}$ and $m_B = 8\text{ kg}$ and possess equal kinetic energies. The ratio of their linear momenta $\dfrac{p_A}{p_B}$ is:
questions.solution:
$$p = \sqrt{2mK} \implies \frac{p_A}{p_B} = \sqrt{\frac{m_A}{m_B}} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{8}} = \frac{1}{2}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A body of mass $5\text{ kg}$ starts from rest under the action of a force $\vec{F} = (10\hat{i} + 15\hat{j})\text{ N}$. The kinetic energy of the body at $t = 2\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
1. $\vec{a} = \frac{\vec{F}}{m} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}\text{ m/s}^2$.
2. $\vec{v}(2) = \vec{a}t = 4\hat{i} + 6\hat{j}\text{ m/s} \implies v^2 = 4^2 + 6^2 = 52\text{ m}^2/\text{s}^2$.
3. Kinetic energy $K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{1}{2}(5)(52) = 130\text{ J}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A ball of mass $m = 0.2\text{ kg}$ moving horizontally with velocity $u = 20\hat{i}\text{ m/s}$ hits a smooth vertical wall and rebounds with velocity $v = -15\hat{i}\text{ m/s}$. If the impact lasts for $\Delta t = 0.01\text{ s}$, the average force exerted by the wall on the ball is:
questions.solution:
1. $\Delta\vec{p} = 0.2(-15\hat{i} - 20\hat{i}) = -7\hat{i}\text{ N}\cdot\text{s}$.
2. $\vec{F}_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\Delta\vec{p}}{\Delta t} = \frac{-7\hat{i}}{0.01} = -700\hat{i}\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The linear momentum $p$ of a body increases by $50\%$. The percentage increase in its kinetic energy is:
questions.solution:
$$K' = \frac{(1.5p)^2}{2m} = 2.25 K \implies \% \text{ increase} = (2.25 - 1) \times 100 = 125\%$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A constant retarding force $F = 50\text{ N}$ is applied to a body of mass $20\text{ kg}$ moving initially with speed $15\text{ m/s}$. The time taken by the body to come to a complete stop is:
questions.solution:
1. Deceleration $a = \frac{F}{m} = \frac{50}{20} = 2.5\text{ m/s}^2$.
2. Time $t = \frac{u}{a} = \frac{15}{2.5} = 6.0\text{ s}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A body of mass $m$ is moving in a circle of radius $R$ with constant angular velocity $\omega$. The rate of change of linear momentum over half a revolution is directed:

options.text: Along the tangent to the path
Toward the center of the circle

questions.solution:
By Newton's second law $\vec{F} = \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt}$. In UCM, the net force is the centripetal force directed strictly toward the center.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: An open rail wagon of mass $M_0 = 1000\text{ kg}$ is coasting freely with velocity $v_0 = 10\text{ m/s}$ along a straight horizontal track. Rain starts falling vertically into the wagon at a constant rate $\mu = 5\text{ kg/s}$. Neglecting friction, the velocity of the wagon after $t = 100\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
Conservation of horizontal momentum: $$M_0 v_0 = (M_0 + \mu t)v(t) \implies 10000 = (1000 + 500)v(t) \implies v(t) = \frac{20}{3} \approx 6.67\text{ m/s}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ is subjected to a force $F(x) = -k x + \beta x^3$. The motion of the particle is:

options.text: Non-harmonic periodic for small oscillations near origin

questions.solution:
The cubic non-linear term $\beta x^3$ prevents the restoring acceleration from being strictly proportional to $-x$, yielding periodic non-harmonic oscillations near the equilibrium point.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A body of mass $m$ is dropped from a height $h$. If air resistance exerts a retarding force proportional to speed ($F_{\text{drag}} = kv$), the terminal velocity of the body is:
questions.solution:
At terminal velocity, net acceleration is zero: $$mg - kv_t = 0 \implies v_t = \frac{mg}{k}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m = 1\text{ kg}$ is moving on the $x$-axis under a conservative force. The potential energy is $U(x) = (x^2 - 4x)\text{ J}$. The magnitude of the force on the block at $x = 5\text{ m}$ is:
questions.solution:
1. $F(x) = -\frac{dU}{dx} = -(2x - 4) = 4 - 2x$.
2. At $x = 5\text{ m}$: $F(5) = 4 - 10 = -6\text{ N} \implies |F| = 6\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A stone of mass $m = 0.5\text{ kg}$ is tied to a string of length $L = 1\text{ m}$ and rotated in a horizontal circle at constant speed $v = 4\text{ m/s}$ on a frictionless table. The net force acting on the stone is:
questions.solution:
$$F_{\text{net}} = \frac{mv^2}{L} = \frac{0.5 \times 4^2}{1} = 8\text{ N (directed towards the center)}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.
